messages:
ana: Heads-up — kicking off a quick sync about the SDK surface for soft-cursor + fallback behavior across Python/TS/Go. We need a minimal API that lets apps handle transient failures without leaking transport details.

mike: +1 — curious what "soft cursor" means in practice here. is it just an opaque resume token or something fancier (idempotency + partial state)?

ana: by "soft cursor" I mean: opaque resume token returned by server that represents a resumable stream snapshot. Not a full session object. Client can pass it back to resume. Server may accept it or reply 410 if expired.

chun: we talked about two behaviors earlier: (A) client-level automatic resume (retry the iterator transparently) vs (B) explicit resume API where caller gets an error with token and decides. Which are we leaning to?

ana: proposal: default to explicit resume API (keep SDK surface simple) but provide opt-in convenience helpers that implement automatic resume with retries/backoff. Rationale: explicit = predictable for platform teams; helpers = convenience for app devs.

mike: that makes sense. For TS/Py we can expose async iterator + a .resume(token) function. For Go we should keep function-based pager that returns (items, resumeToken, err). That maps idiomatically.

chun: important: how do retries interact with idempotency? If automatic resume retries, we need server guarantees that resuming is safe (no duplicates) or the SDK must de-duplicate. We can't shift heavy semantics into SDK.

ana: agreed. Server contract: resume token = at-least-once semantics by default. If consumer needs exactly-once semantics they should use request-id idempotency window header. We'll document that.

sara: telemetry question: if we add automatic resume helpers, we must emit events: resume_attempt, resume_success, resume_failure, token_expired. Ops teams need to correlate these with route/tenant.

infra-bot: deploy:soft-cursor-service v2 rolled to canary (us-east1). Logs show resume-token TTL = 5m by default.

mike: TTL is relevant. For short-lived retries TTL 5m OK. For long pollers it might be too short. Can we make TTL configurable per route?

ana: server will support per-route TTL and a max-retry window. SDK helpers should respect route-provided TTL in response metadata (e.g., header x-resume-ttl-ms). If header missing, fall back to 5m.

chun: edge case: streaming -> page conversion. If a stream fails mid-chunk, resume token points to token+offset. SDK helper needs to rehydrate the partial item state. That's messy.

ana: agree — don't attempt item-level rehydration in SDK. If server can't provide whole-item resumes, helper should fail and surface token so caller can decide to re-fetch page with stricter semantics.

sara: for Python & TS ergonomics: propose APIs:
- async iterator model: for await (const item of client.listFoos(opts)) {}  (auto-resume disabled by default)
- client.listFoosPager(opts) returns {items: AsyncIterable, resume: (token) => void} or helper combine.
- convenience: client.withAutoResume(listCall, {retries, backoff}) returns iterator that retries transparently.

mike: Go sketch: func ListFoos(ctx, opts) (Pager, error) where Pager.Next() (Foo, error) and Pager.Resume(token) error. Auto-resume helper func AutoPager(ctx, opts) (chan Foo, chan error) maybe too clunky. Simpler: provide a wrapper in go-sdks/pkg/helpers.AutoPager(pager) that returns channel.

chun: backoff defaults? we should align across languages: jittered exponential with max attempts = 5, base = 100ms, max = 2s. But helpers should allow override and support deadline propagation.

ana: yes — tie to context/deadline where possible. If ctx.Done triggers, stop retries and return last token if present.

mike: docs: we need clear diagrams showing error flows: transient error -> helper retries -> success; transient error + expired token -> returns ResumeRequired with token; permanent 4xx -> bubble up. Also include quick migration snippets for users currently relying on transparent retry.

sara: tests: add e2e for: "resume succeeds after server hiccup", "resume token expired" and "partial-item failure surfaces token not rehydrated". Also unit tests for telemetry emitted.

chun: question about transport specifics: Should resume token be sent in request body or header? Header is simpler for proxies but body is idempotent-friendly. Thoughts?

ana: use header X-Resume-Token for initial resume attempts (keeps body unchanged). Also include resume_token in response body for clients that prefer it. Server to accept both.

mike: rollout plan:
- phase 1: add server support + header metadata + minimal SDK surface to return token (no auto helpers). Publish doc RFC.
- phase 2: implement auto-resume helpers in Py/TS and helper package for Go. Feature-flag them off by default.
- phase 3: enable for small set of routes, collect telemetry, iterate TTL/backoff.

ana: compatibility: mark helper APIs experimental for one minor release before graduating. Deprecation path for older opaque cursor APIs: create shim that translates old tokens to new format server-side for a migration window.

sara: security: resume tokens must be cryptographically opaque and scoped to route+tenant to avoid token replay across routes. Add that to threat model.

chun: last: error shape. We should add a typed error class (ResumeRequiredError) that includes .resumeToken and .reason. That maps well to TS/Py/Go idioms.

mike: +1. In Go error type implement interface ResumeToken() string.

ana: ok I'll draft the follow-up RFC with API sketches and tests. Action items:
- ana: RFC + diagrams + examples (due EOW)
- mike: TS + Py helper prototypes (POC next week)
- chun: Go helper shim design + error interface (POC mid next week)
- sara: telemetry + e2e test cases (writeup)

mike: :thumbsup: thanks — one more: add example of how to opt-in to auto-resume in client config (single flag) so platform teams can enforce policy.

ana: noted. I'll include.

infra-bot: note: canary metrics show 0.3% resume attempts per 1k requests for listFoos in us-east1.

sara: good enough signal for rollout. stopping here.

mike: thanks all. Follow-up in RFC thread.
